newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay blue-chips end shade higher in mixed trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay blue-chips end shade higher in mixed trade.

text.p: Shares at Bombay bourses edged up by close of trade on Friday with a lack of major market-moving news limiting price movement, dealers said.
"There were very few active players in the market..nothing much to talk about," said a dealer at a domestic brokerage.
"It was a sleepy day for prices," he added.
Absence of foreign funds, the big players in the market and cautiousness among local operators after Wednesday's 6.0 percent rally helped limit volatility in the market, traders said.
The Congress Parliamentary Party was due to meet at 4 p.m. (1030 GMT) to elect a new leader to replace former premier P.V. Narasimha Rao.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's 30-share index closed 38.76 points up at 3,264.0, after hitting the day's low of 3,204.88.
Rao who stepped down as Congress party president in September after facing immense pressure from senior party leaders resigned from his last post as parliamentary party chief last month.
The selection of a new Congress parliamentary leader assumes importance as Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority coaltion depends on the Congress for make or break support.
Analysts said the market had largely discounted the election of a new leader, with action focussed on economic news.
Market sentiments got a boost after the government on Tuesday said it would shortly announce a series of policies to boost industrial growth and revive sagging capital markets.
The index rallied about 6.0 percent on Wednesday.
On Friday, infrastructure stock, BHEL and telecom stock MTNL surged on short-covering by operators, dealers said.

BHEL rose 11.0 rupees, or 5.15 percent, to 224.75 and MTNL 1.75 to 235.75. SBI was up 0.75 to 241.75, ACC 14.75 to 1,289.0, Gujarat Ambuja 8.0 to 248.75, Reliance 2.25 to 215.50 and TISCO 0.50 to 180.0. REUTER
